os-net.title: Links and email
os-net.summary: Check and clean links, edit their query safely, tell whether two links are the same page, and turn an email into a stable comparison key.

gives.1: Accept only plain http and https links, with no login in them, and fix a link someone typed without its scheme.
gives.2: Add or remove query parameters without letting a value inject new ones, and drop tracking parameters.
gives.3: Compare links and emails by a key, so the same page or mailbox written two ways is found as one.

sample.link-key: Recognize the same link written two ways
sample.mail-key: Turn an email into a comparison key

urls.title: Links
urls.summary: Validate, clean, edit and compare links.

1.title: Safe links
1.text: `UrlEx.IsUrl` accepts only absolute `http` and `https` links with no login in them.

2.title: Fix a link
2.text: `TryNormalize` adds `https://` when the scheme is missing.

3.title: Compare links
3.text: `Key` and `AreSame` ignore tracking parameters, `www.` and case.

4.title: Safe query edits
4.text: Values you add with `WithQuery` are escaped.

1.title: Checking and fixing
1.text:
`UrlEx.IsUrl` accepts only absolute `http` and `https` links of at most 2048 characters with no user name or password in them.

`TryNormalize` also adds `https://` when the scheme is missing and returns the canonical form.

2.title: Editing the query
2.text:
`WithQuery` and `WithoutQuery` edit the query string without decoding what is already there. Every value you add is escaped, so a value such as `a&admin=1` stays one value.

`TrackingKeys` lists the standard `utm_` parameters.

3.title: Comparing and showing
3.text:
`Key` turns a link into a SHA-256 key. The key ignores the scheme, `www.`, case, a trailing slash and tracking parameters. `AreSame` compares two links by that key.

`Readable` decodes UTF-8 escapes such as Persian letters for display. It leaves characters like `%2F` encoded.

4.title: Short code, site and status
4.text:
`UrlToken` checks the short codes used in short links.

`UrlPlatform` names the site a link belongs to, using a host table you can replace.

`StatusOf` folds an HTTP status into a `UrlStatus`.

check.title: Check that a text is a safe link
check.note: Only http and https pass, and a link with a login in it is refused.

normalize.title: Fix a link typed without its scheme
normalize.note: Other schemes such as javascript are refused.

query.title: Add and remove query parameters
query.note: The value a&b=c stays one value, and the fragment is kept.

same-link.title: Compare two links by their key
same-link.note: The key is 64 hex characters, so it is safe to store and index.

readable.title: Show a link in a readable form
readable.note: Escaped UTF-8 text is decoded; a space stays %20.

token.title: Check the short code of a link
token.note: Codes may only use a to z and 0 to 9, and a set of words such as api and admin is reserved. Pass your own words as the second argument.

platform.title: Name the site a link belongs to
platform.note: The default table knows a few common sites. Pass your own table to teach it more.

status.title: Turn an HTTP status into a link status
status.note: Any 2xx is Ok, any 3xx is Redirected, 404 and 410 are NotFound, other 4xx are BadRequest and 5xx is Failed.

parse.title: Parse a link into its parts
parse.note: The link is normalized first, and the key ignores tracking parameters.

type.UrlEx: Link helpers: validation, normalization, query editing, comparison keys, host matching and status mapping.
type.UrlToken: Rules for the short code of a link: allowed characters and reserved words.
type.UrlPlatform: Names the site a link belongs to from a table of hosts.
type.UrlStatus: The state of a link, after checking it.
type.UrlInfo: A link split into its parts: the normalized address, host, path, query and comparison key.

UrlEx.MaxLength: The longest link that is accepted, 2048 characters.
UrlEx.TrackingKeys: The standard utm_ parameters, compared without regard to case.
UrlEx.IsUrl: True for an absolute http or https link with no login in it.
UrlEx.TryNormalize: Trims the text, adds https:// when there is no scheme, and returns the canonical link.
UrlEx.IsHost: True when a host equals the given host or is a subdomain of it.
UrlEx.WithQuery: Adds or replaces query parameters. Values are escaped and existing text is not decoded.
UrlEx.Key: A SHA-256 key of the link that ignores scheme, www, case, trailing slash and tracking parameters.
UrlEx.AreSame: True when two links have the same key.
UrlEx.Readable: Decodes UTF-8 escapes for display. ASCII escapes stay encoded.
UrlEx.TryGetFileName: Reads the file name from the path of a link.
UrlEx.StatusOf: Maps an HTTP status code to a UrlStatus.

UrlToken.Reserved: Words that can't be used as a short code.
UrlToken.Normalize: Trims and lowercases a code. Empty text gives null.
UrlToken.IsWellFormed: True when the code has only a to z and 0 to 9.
UrlToken.IsReserved: True for a reserved word or one of the extra words you pass.

UrlPlatform.Defaults: The built-in table of hosts and the names they map to.
UrlPlatform.Detect: The name for the link's host, or null. Pass a table to replace the default one.

UrlInfo.TryParse: Normalizes the text and splits it, or returns false.
UrlInfo.Query: The query without the question mark.
UrlInfo.IsHost: True when the host equals the given host or is a subdomain of it.

mail.title: Email
mail.summary: Check an email address and build a key that makes two spellings of one mailbox equal.

1.title: One check
1.text: The address is first checked with `RegexEx.IsEmail` from OS.Core.

2.title: Comparison key
2.text: `Key` makes spellings of the same mailbox equal.

3.title: Masked form
3.text: A `Masked` form is built for screens and logs.

4.title: No exception
4.text: A bad address gives the `Invalid` status, not an exception.

1.title: Check and result
1.text:
`MailEx.Normalize` first checks the address with `RegexEx.IsEmail` from OS.Core, so there is one email check in the whole stack.

When the address is valid, the result carries a `MailNormalized`. It has a comparison `Key`, the `User` and `Host` it was built from, a `Masked` form for screens and logs, and a `MailType`.

2.title: Building the key
2.text:
The key is meant for finding duplicates, not for sending mail.

It lowercases the name and maps `googlemail.com` to `gmail.com`. It removes dots for Gmail. It cuts the `+tag` part for providers known to support tags.

3.title: Keeping and tuning
3.text:
Keep the address the person typed and store the key beside it. Each rule can be switched off with `MailOptions`.

A bad address returns the `Invalid` status with the code `net.mail.invalid`. No exception is thrown.

normalize.title: Build the comparison key of an address
normalize.note: GoogleMail and Gmail are the same mailbox, dots do not count in Gmail and +news is a tag.

options.title: Switch a rule off
options.note: Outlook ignores the part after +, but the dots in its names count.

mask.title: Show an address without exposing it
mask.note: The mask keeps the first and last letters of the name. A company domain is marked Corporate.

invalid.title: Handle an invalid address
invalid.note: Check the code, not a message; the code never changes.

type.MailOptions: Which normalization rules to apply. All are on by default.
type.MailNormalized: The result of a successful normalization.
type.MailType: Whether the address belongs to a personal provider, a company or a throwaway service.
type.NetCodes: The error codes of this package.

MailEx.Normalize: Validates the address and returns its key, parts, mask and type, or an Invalid result.

MailOptions.RemoveDots: Remove dots from the name for Gmail. On by default.
MailOptions.RemoveTags: Cut the +tag part for providers that support it. On by default.
MailOptions.LowerCase: Lowercase the name. On by default.
MailOptions.NormHost: Map alternative hosts such as googlemail.com to the main one. On by default.
MailOptions.ExtraTempHosts: More hosts to treat as temporary, added to the built-in list. Compared without regard to case.

MailNormalized.Key: The comparison key. Don't use it as the address to send to.
MailNormalized.Masked: The address with the middle of the name hidden.

NetCodes.MailInvalid: The address is not a valid email.
